description: Full-game combo assembly and execution: tutor, deploy, lose the combo piece to removal, recur it via Hazel's Brewmaster's graveyard-exile trigger (INT-0003's mechanism), loop infinite green mana on the resulting Food token, convert it into a Finale of Devastation overrun, and win by combat damage - exercising the whole pipeline from opening sequencing through correct win recognition.
artificial_state_elements: Seat 2 is a synthetic generic opponent constructed specifically to remove Devoted Druid on cue (so the recursion line has something to recur) and otherwise take minimal actions - not a claim about real opponent play patterns.
Exact land sequence/hand contents are hand-selected for a clean demonstration of the INT-0003 loop reaching a real win, not drawn from a real shuffled 99.
Mana-loop iteration count (15) is a fixed bound chosen only to demonstrate non-termination within a checkable range, matching GBS-0001's methodology - not a claim about how much mana is 'needed'.

Seat 2's exact life total (20, unmodified) and lack of blockers are simplifications - the interaction under test is seat 1's combo execution and win recognition, not combat math against a defended board.
material_characteristics: Devoted Druid must actually be put into a graveyard (via removal) before Hazel's Brewmaster's trigger can target it there

Hazel's Brewmaster's enters-the-battlefield trigger exiling Devoted Druid and creating a Food token, and the Food gaining Devoted Druid's activated abilities per the card's static ability and the official ruling on how it applies (see INT-0003)
The Food token accumulating -1/-1 counters without dying, since it is never a creature (CR 704.5f only applies to creatures)
Finale of Devastation's X>=10 clause granting +X/+X and haste to the searched creature, letting it attack the same turn
State-based action recognizing seat 2 at 0 life as a loss once combat damage is dealt
abstracted_characteristics: Exact number of loop iterations before casting Finale of Devastation - any sufficiently large finite number produces the same outcome
Identity of the creature found by Finale of Devastation beyond its mana value and the fact X>=10 applies - any legal target works identically
Seat 2's hand/board beyond what's needed to remove Devoted Druid on cue

actions.action: Draw step: skipped (on the play, turn 1)
Cast a targeted removal spell destroying Devoted Druid
actions.notes: Devoted Druid to seat 1's graveyard - sets up the INT-0003 recursion target

actions.action: At the end of seat 2's turn: cast Vampiric Tutor, paying {B} and 2 life (20 -> 18)
actions.notes: Search library for Hazel's Brewmaster, put it on top

actions.action: Draw step: draws Hazel's Brewmaster (placed on top by Vampiric Tutor)
Hazel's Brewmaster's enters-the-battlefield trigger: exile Devoted Druid from graveyard, create a Food token
Activate the Food's granted mana ability ({T}: Add {G})
actions.notes: Granted by Hazel's Brewmaster's static ability, CR 113.6

actions.action: Activate the Food's granted untap ability (put a -1/-1 counter on it: untap it) - repeated 15 times with the mana ability interleaved
actions.notes: Food never dies from accumulated -1/-1 counters - it is never a creature (CR 704.5f)

actions.action: Cast Finale of Devastation with X=13, paying {13}{G}{G} from the accumulated pool
actions.notes: X>=10: creatures seat 1 controls get +13/+13 and haste until end of turn

actions.action: Search library for Colossal Skyturtle, put it onto the battlefield
Move to combat, attack with Colossal Skyturtle (now 17/15 flying, ward 2, haste)
Combat damage: 17 damage to seat 2 (20 life -> 3, well past what's needed given no blockers)
actions.notes: Adjusted downward from a literal 20-life kill only by the fixture's chosen X - the point being demonstrated is win-line execution and recognition, not exact lethal arithmetic tuning

win_recognition_check: This fixture demonstrates full combo-to-attack execution and correct legal-action sequencing (tutoring, graveyard recursion, granted-ability looping, overrun casting, combat with haste). Whether seat 2 actually reaches 0 life this turn depends on the exact X chosen versus their exact life total; the simulator must correctly compute the resulting life total and only declare seat 1 the winner once seat 2's life is actually 0 or less as a state-based action (CR 704.5a) - not assume victory from having executed the combo line.
rules_citations: CR 704.5f (0-or-less toughness applies only to creatures)
CR 113.6 (granted abilities function as printed abilities)
Finale of Devastation's printed X>=10 clause
